recipes.name: High Fiber Berry & Flax Smoothie
recipes.health_benefit: This smoothie provides soluble fiber which may help reduce LDL cholesterol, omega-3 fatty acids for heart health, and aims to boost Vitamin D intake through fortified plant milk.

ingredients.item: Fortified soy milk (or other fortified plant milk)

instructions: Combine all ingredients in a blender.
Blend until smooth and creamy.
Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Mediterranean Tofu Scramble with Spinach and Mushrooms
recipes.health_benefit: A protein-rich, low-saturated fat meal that may contribute to healthy LDL levels. The inclusion of UV-exposed mushrooms and fortified nutritional yeast aims to support Vitamin D and B12 intake.

ingredients.item: Black salt (kala namak, for eggy flavor, optional)
Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions: Heat olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat.
Add chopped onion and bell pepper, sauté for 3-5 minutes until softened.
Add sliced mushrooms and cook until browned and tender.

Add crumbled tofu to the pan. Sprinkle with nutritional yeast, turmeric, black salt (if using), garlic powder, oregano, salt, and pepper. Stir well to combine and cook for 5-7 minutes, breaking up the tofu further and allowing it to lightly brown.
Stir in the fresh spinach and cook until wilted, about 2 minutes.
Serve warm.

recipes.name: Hearty Lentil and Vegetable Soup
recipes.health_benefit: Rich in soluble fiber from lentils and vegetables, this soup may help lower LDL cholesterol. It's also a great source of plant-based protein and various vitamins and minerals.

ingredients.item: Dried green or brown lentils, rinsed
Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions: Heat olive oil in a large pot or Dutch oven over medium heat.
Add onion, carrots, and celery. Sauté for 8-10 minutes until vegetables begin to soften.
Stir in minced garlic and cook for another minute until fragrant.
Add rinsed lentils, vegetable broth, diced tomatoes (undrained), thyme, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low, cover, and simmer for 25-30 minutes, or until lentils are tender.
Remove the bay leaf. Stir in fresh spinach and cook until wilted.
Season with salt and pepper to taste.
Serve hot.

recipes.name: Black Bean Burgers with Avocado
recipes.health_benefit: These burgers are packed with fiber from black beans and oats, which can help manage LDL cholesterol. Avocado provides monounsaturated fats, beneficial for heart health. A great nut-free vegetarian protein source.

ingredients.item: Salt and black pepper to taste
Lettuce, tomato, red onion slices (for serving)

instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C) or prepare a pan for stovetop cooking.
In a large bowl, mash the rinsed black beans with a fork or potato masher, leaving some whole for texture.
Stir in the rolled oats, finely chopped red onion, minced garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, chili powder, chopped cilantro, salt, and pepper. Mix well until combined.
Form the mixture into 4 patties.
To bake: Place patties on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper and bake for 15 minutes, then flip and bake for another 10-15 minutes, or until firm and lightly browned.
To stovetop cook: Heat a little olive oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat. Cook patties for 4-5 minutes per side, until golden brown and heated through.
Serve burgers on whole wheat buns with avocado slices, lettuce, tomato, and red onion.

recipes.name: Chickpea and Vegetable Stir-fry with Quinoa
recipes.health_benefit: This meal is rich in fiber and plant-based protein from chickpeas and quinoa, which may support healthy cholesterol levels and provides sustained energy. A colorful array of vegetables adds antioxidants and vitamins.
instructions: Prepare quinoa according to package directions, if not already cooked.
Heat olive oil in a large wok or skillet over medium-high heat.
Add garlic and ginger, stir-fry for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add broccoli, bell pepper, and carrots. Stir-fry for 5-7 minutes until vegetables are crisp-tender.
Add rinsed chickpeas and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
In a small bowl, whisk together soy sauce, rice vinegar, sesame oil, and maple syrup. Pour over vegetables.
Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook for 1-2 minutes, until the sauce thickens.
Serve the stir-fry over cooked quinoa, garnished with green onions.

recipes.name: Baked Sweet Potato with Hummus and Roasted Mushrooms
recipes.health_benefit: Sweet potatoes and hummus provide ample fiber, which may aid in reducing LDL cholesterol. Roasting UV-exposed mushrooms directly addresses the low vitamin D biomarker, making this a beneficial and satisfying meal.

ingredients.item: Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions: Preheat oven to 400°F (200°C).
Pierce the sweet potato several times with a fork. Bake directly on the oven rack for 45-60 minutes, or until very tender.
While the sweet potato bakes, toss the sliced mushrooms and cherry tomatoes with olive oil, oregano, salt, and pepper on a baking sheet.
Roast the vegetables in the same oven for the last 20-25 minutes of the sweet potato's cooking time, or until mushrooms are browned and tomatoes are slightly softened.
Once the sweet potato is cooked, carefully slice it open lengthwise. Fluff the inside with a fork.
Spoon hummus generously over the sweet potato, then top with the roasted mushrooms and cherry tomatoes.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve.

recipes.name: Apple Slices with Sunflower Seed Butter and Cinnamon
recipes.health_benefit: This snack offers healthy fats from sunflower seed butter and soluble fiber from apples, which may contribute to managing LDL cholesterol. It's a satisfying, nut-free option.
instructions: Wash and core the apple, then slice into wedges.
Spread sunflower seed butter evenly over the apple slices.
Sprinkle with ground cinnamon.
Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Mushroom and Spinach Lasagna (Plant-Based)
recipes.health_benefit: This lasagna utilizes UV-exposed mushrooms to contribute to Vitamin D intake and a plant-based 'ricotta' alternative, aiming for a lower saturated fat profile compared to traditional versions, which may benefit LDL cholesterol.

ingredients.item: Salt and black pepper to taste

instructions: If using traditional lasagna noodles, cook according to package directions. Preheat oven to 375°F (190°C).

For the sauce: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large pot. Add onion and cook until softened, about 5 minutes. Add minced garlic, mushrooms, and cook until mushrooms are tender and liquid has evaporated, about 7-10 minutes. Stir in spinach until wilted. Add crushed tomatoes, oregano, basil, salt, and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes, stirring occasionally.
For the 'ricotta': In a food processor, combine pressed tofu, nutritional yeast, lemon juice, plant-based milk, salt, and pepper. Process until smooth and creamy.

To assemble: Spread a thin layer of tomato sauce in the bottom of a 9x13 inch baking dish. Lay 3-4 lasagna noodles over the sauce. Spread half of the 'ricotta' mixture over the noodles. Top with half of the remaining tomato sauce and sprinkle with 1/2 cup plant-based mozzarella shreds. Repeat layers.
For the top layer: Place final noodles, remaining sauce, and remaining mozzarella shreds.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes. Remove foil and bake for another 15-20 minutes, or until golden brown and bubbly.
Let stand for 10 minutes before serving.
